reasoned_checks.conclusion: Journal insert, revision-fenced tombstone update and reaction cleanup are now in one batch. The cleanup exception propagates; the SQL engine adapter rolls back the full transaction. The real migrations and current handler use identical message/sender/revision guards. No separate cleanup remains on the new-delete success path.

The matched operation branch first checks message/kind/expected revision/request digest, then retries guarded cleanup only for an existing sender-owned tombstone. Cleanup errors propagate rather than returning deduplicated success. Stable row, revision, operation journal and resource bytes are retained.

Reaction INSERT and DELETE recheck participant and non-deleted state atomically inside their SQL statement. A final target read rejects a tombstone after the initial read. Race tests suspend immediately before actual SQL, perform delete, then resume; assertions detect both resurrection and false success. A deletion occurring after the final live observation is a later concurrent operation, not something this snapshot can promise to prevent.

The adapter prepares and executes the actual production SQL with bound arguments in node:sqlite, loads all three real messaging migrations, enables foreign keys, and performs a real file-database reopen. Hooks only pause before statements/batches or throw after commit. There is no canned mutation result. A trigger raises an actual SQLite cleanup failure. This validates SQL/handler behavior once executed, but does not emulate every D1 backend/runtime property or qualify deployed D1.

Legacy rows exist before additive extension/mutation migrations. Assertions preserve message ID, revision initialization, body, nonce, read timestamp and resource metadata; foreign-key rejection is exercised. Delete recovery explicitly retains resources while clearing references/reactions.

PATCH/DELETE/reaction routes invoke these handlers. SQLite tests generate signed fixture tokens and invoke actual handlers. They do not exercise production RS256 account-service binding or external middleware.
